scenario: [LCRS.6.6.1]: a `CallError` that no superseding call retracts lives exactly `CallError`'s TTL, 5_min ([LCRS.4.2.1]), and no other lifetime. The host delivers one `CallError`, corr `c1`, at t=0, and no call follows to supersede it. A probe asserted at t=299.999999999s sees it, so `seen` logs "error 1"; a probe asserted at t=300s exactly does not, because the pump retracts a fact due at the current instant before anything fires ([RARC.5.2.4], [RARC.5.6.3]). Exactly ["error 1"]. Each break moves the log: a shorter lifetime loses the line; no expiry, a longer one, or a sweep that keeps a fact due now adds "error 2". `CallError`'s TTL is independent of any response schema's, and the program's one service is `no response`, so one lifetime applied to both kinds cannot pass this and its twin, LCRS.6.6.1_response_expires_at_its_schema_ttl, together. PATH PINNED: the pump-entry TTL sweep over a host-asserted `CallError` -- libds `ds_engine_sweep_ttl_via_wrappers`, Mercury `ds.engine.sweep_expired`.
rules_ds:
service svc.read:
    kwarg n: Int
    no response

schema Probe scope explicit:
    k: Int

rule seen:
    Probe p
    CallError
->
    log info "error {p.k}"
